new_packages.label: אֱמוּנָה, מִצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת וּתְפִלָּה

proposed_edges.source: שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת אֱמוּנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: כָּל מִצְו‍ֹתֶיךָ אֱמוּנָה
וֶאֱמוּנָה זֶה תְּפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם: פְּרִישָׂן בִּצְלּוֹ

new_packages.reason: This package emerges from three explicit bechina statements the Rebbe makes in the source text, forming a connected chain of shared-nature identities. (1) Moses's hands (יָדָיו) = practical commandments (מצוות מעשיות) — the Rebbe interprets 'וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה' by saying 'יָדָיו – הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת מִצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת'. Hands are the embodiment of practical deed — they ARE the domain of practical commandments. (2) Practical commandments (מצוות מעשיות) = faith (אמונה) — the Rebbe cites 'כָּל מִצְוֹתֶיךָ אֱמוּנָה' (Tehilim 119:86) and states 'שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת אֱמוּנָה'. Practical commandments are not the vehicle of faith — they ARE faith. This is a symmetric bechina identification. (3) Faith (אמונה) = prayer (תפלה) — 'וֶאֱמוּנָה זֶה תְּפִלָּה'. The targum's translation of Moses's hands as 'פְּרִישָׂן בִּצְלּוֹ' (spreading in prayer) confirms the identity. Faith-as-supplication is the same reality as prayer-as-faith. These three bechinas form a coherent, independent good domain: embodied holy action (ידיו/מצוות מעשיות) in its essential nature is faith (אמונה), and faith in its active, vocal expression is prayer (תפלה). This cluster is the polar mirror of Package 1 (Amalek/philosophers) — where Package 1 represents the evil force that operates on natural reason without fear of God, this package represents the good force that transcends nature through faith and embodied commandment. The Torah's eitza flow confirms they are opposing forces: through אמונה ומצוות מעשיות, Amalek (Package 1) is weakened. But the nodes' essential natures are bechina within this cluster, not eitza between them.

observations:
Torah #19 (LM2) is one of the shorter Torahs in the collection, with only 3 bechina edges recorded in the dataset. However, the source text contains a significantly richer bechina structure than what is currently captured. The dataset correctly recorded the evil cluster (Amalek/philosophers/stumbling-block) and the telos cluster (תכלית/סוף דבר), but missed a central good cluster of four concepts explicitly linked by bechina language.

The newly proposed Package 3 (אמונה/מצוות מעשיות/תפלה/ידיו) is not a border case — all three bechina connections are stated with the Rebbe's standard bechina vocabulary: 'הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת', 'בְּחִינַת', and 'זֶה'. This cluster is structurally distinct from Package 2 (תכלית/תמימות): Package 2 describes the goal (ultimate purpose / simplicity as the endpoint), while Package 3 describes the means in their essential identity (faith = commandments = prayer as different faces of the same spiritual reality). They relate to each other by eitza (the faith-cluster leads to the telos-cluster), not by bechina — hence they are correctly kept as separate packages.

The Torah's mirror structure: Package 1 (evil: Amalek and philosophy) ↔ Package 3 (good: faith and prayer) is the central polarity of the teaching. Package 2 (telos/simplicity) functions as the culmination toward which the good side aims. The eitza spine is: [Package 3: אמונה/מצוות] → weakens [Package 1: עמלק/פילוסופים] → thereby achieving [Package 2: תכלית/סוף דבר].
